text:
marta: Heads up — I reproduced a double-evict during a prefix handoff + background eviction race. Repro notes below, stack snippets and logs included. Anyone else hit this?

marta: repro steps:
- tenant A pinned to shard X, handoff starts to shard Y (handoff: send revoke -> await ack -> transfer metadata)
- concurrently eviction worker on X runs and sees lease revoked but still holds residency -> does physical remove
- handoff finishes and the receiver re-creates prefix, but some in-flight ops reference freed pointers -> use-after-free / assertion failures

marta: logs excerpt:
```
[2026-03-18T21:12:03Z] handoff: send_revoke prefix=tz-42 owner=X epoch=102
[2026-03-18T21:12:03Z] evict_worker: start_evict prefix=tz-42 lease_epoch=102
[2026-03-18T21:12:03Z] handoff: ack_revoke prefix=tz-42
[2026-03-18T21:12:03Z] evict_worker: physical_delete prefix=tz-42
[2026-03-18T21:12:04Z] handoff: complete_receive prefix=tz-42 -> create_residency prefix=tz-42 owner=Y epoch=103
[2026-03-18T21:12:04Z] runtime: crash use-after-free at kv::read
```

alex: saw a canary with similar symptoms last week. My quick take: we need a stronger handoff/evict coordination primitive — epoch alone is necessary but not sufficient for races with in-flight ops and async prefetch.

alex: proposal A (cheap): attach a short-lived "handoff token" to the eviction attempt. Handoff includes token in the revoke header. Receiver will accept prefills/rebinds that present the same token so in-flight operations can reattach. If token mismatch, treat as new object. Token is GC'd after timeout.

jia: token idea is elegant but still has corner cases: what if token GC happens before slow op finishes? Also prefetches that cross reorders could lose token. I'd prefer tombstone + delayed physical delete: on revoke we write tombstone {lease_epoch, owner_id, tombstone_ts}. Eviction marks tombstone but physical delete only after tombstone_ts+grace_period AND verify current epoch != tombstone. That ensures receiver won't see freed memory while still letting GC proceed.

shaun: tombstone works correctness-wise but increases metadata churn and read-path checks. For high-throughput hot prefixes it might pressure the allocator. Token approach is lower overhead but requires solid metrics and careful GC.

marta: both options have tradeoffs: tombstone = safer, simpler semantics; token = lower steady-state cost but more complex GC/attaching logic. We also need a hybrid for hot keys (fast-path).

alex: hybrid: on revoke, if entry hot (accessed in last N ms) convert to soft-evict (mark as demoted, keep in memory) and postpone physical delete. Cold entries get token/tombstone flow. That keeps latency low for hot traffic.

jia: agree on hot fast-path. Also want explicit unit+stress tests: simulate revoke+long prefetch pause. Add an integration chaos test that pauses handoff ack mid-flight and runs concurrent evict loops.

shaun: implementation plan suggestion:
- step 1 (short): implement handshake token + attach handlers, add metrics (token_attach, token_rebind, token_gc). Canary to prefix-stage.
- step 2 (medium): add soft-evict fast-path for hot entries.
- step 3 (long): tombstone-based GC as fallback if token approach shows correctness gaps under stress.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary patch 265.1 deployed to prefix-stage at 2026-03-19T15:42Z (monitored).

marta: sounds good. Couple of open questions: token format (uuid vs monotonic counter), token lifetime and what metrics we need to alert on token_rebind > 0.5% of ops, and rate-limit tombstone promotions to avoid metadata storms.

alex: token = 128-bit random (uuid) to avoid cross-shard counter coordination. Lifetime = 30s default, configurable per-pool. Metrics: token_attach_rate, token_rebind_rate, token_gc_duration, tombstone_promote_rate.

jia: for tombstone GC we should gate by cluster-wide low-pressure signal (mem_pressure < threshold) or per-shard watermark to avoid cascading deletes during mem pressure. Also record tombstone_latency_percentiles.

shaun: i'll prototype token attach API today and wire a small GC worker stub. I'll add a test harness that runs the chaos scenario.

marta: Action items: alex implement token handshake + metrics PR; jia draft tombstone fallback design with GC gating; shaun prototype token GC + chaos test; i'll schedule sync friday 9am PST to review results. tagging: @alex @jia @shaun. :thumbsup:

marta: leaving this thread open for PR links and short canary reports, please paste them here.
